findings: DEC-122 propagated to the Énoncé (l.554–558, p. 241): read over all Hausdorff connected affine conical manifolds of Benzécri dimension n ≥ 3, the « isomorphisme fonctoriel » is false whatever the reading of « isomorphisme », because the essential image of F is exactly the cones with a proper ℝ₊*-action: Cone/Counterexample's ConeCex.VDim m (Hausdorff, second countable, connected) is isomorphic to no F(B) with B Hausdorff (Benzecri.not_essSurjAsPrinted_dim, against the Prop EssSurjAsPrintedDim). In dimension n ≤ 2 the printed form holds (essSurjAsPrinted_of_le_one).

F(B) always has a proper ℝ₊*-action and a Hausdorff base (FCone.properSMul, FCone.t2Space_coneBase): the construction of the proof (l.560–649) never produces a cone outside DEC-122's corrected category, so the correction loses nothing on the projective side.
questions: Marking: the equivalence is proved with 0 sorry over DEC-124's objects (proper cones), but that is an added hypothesis relative to the printed Énoncé; may it be MARKED in its corrected form as DEC-124 did for § 2 Prop. 2? (Left unmarked, status partial.)
« φ ∘ j₂ = j₁ » (l.640, p. 242) is read as composition in diagrammatic order (j₁ = j₂ ∘ germ φ), as in « J(V₂)∘f » (p. 238); confirm.

« FJ(B) s'identifie avec J₁(F(B)) » (l.568, l.604) is a remark inside the proof and is not formalized as a bijection FJ(B) ≃ J₁(F(B)); its global form for B = V/ℝ₊* is ConeBase.unitMap (V ≅ F(V/ℝ₊*)). Is a separate formalization wanted?
